messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [redacted]

Age: 56 years

Gender: Male

Admission Date: [redacted]

Discharge Date: [redacted]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with subjective fever, body aches, nonproductive cough, left-sided pleuritic chest pain, and recurrent infected skin cyst with MRSA. Physical examination revealed coarse breath sounds with no wheezing, and a thick purulence was exposed from the cyst. Radiographic and CT studies showed developments of multifocal regions of nodular appearing infiltration within both lungs. Blood culture resulted in positive with MRSA that grew with different antibiotic sensitivities. Despite being on the antibiotic/vancomycin, the patient continued to be bacteremic with MRSA, and repeated chest CT scan revealed the progression of lung pneumonia and multiple new nodules. Further TEE revealed a large vegetation was involving the pulmonic valve that was adherent to the artery itself. The patient underwent pulmonary valve replacement using a LivaNova extra-large sutureless valve. Tissue valve culture came back positive for MRSA, and the patient was discharged home on IV vancomycin for six weeks.

Hospital Course Summary:
The patient was admitted with a history of recurrent infected skin cyst with MRSA, subjective fever, body aches, nonproductive cough, and left-sided pleuritic chest pain. Workup revealed MRSA Pulmonary Valve Endocarditis, and the patient underwent a pulmonary valve replacement. After a total of six weeks of IV vancomycin therapy, the patient was discharged home.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The principal diagnosis is MRSA pulmonary valve endocarditis. In ICD-10-AM, infective endocarditis is coded to I33 (acute and subacute endocarditis), with B95.6 or a similar code added for the organism. A separate category exists for pulmonary valve endocarditis, I39 (endocarditis and heart valve disorders in diseases classified elsewhere), but it is a dagger/asterisk-type code. Bacterial endocarditis with sepsis could be coded to A41, but the dominant condition here is the endocarditis, and I33 is the standard category for it.

I33
